newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban say they capture Bagram airbase, Charikar.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say they capture Bagram airbase, Charikar.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia captured a key military airbase and a town north of Kabul in a big offensive on Thursday, Taleban sources said.
The sources said Taleban fighters had seized the Bagram military airbase and the town of Charikar, about 50 km (31 miles) north of the Afghan capital in heavy fighting.
Wounded fighters on the Taleban side of the front line said both sides had suffered heavy casualties in the fighting.
"Bagram air base was captured late this morning and Charikar city has also come under our control," said one fighter.
No independent account of the battle, which followed three days of inconclusive U.N.-sponsored peace talks between the Taleban and its opponents, was immediately available.

The Soviet-built Bagram airbase and the town of Charikar had been in the hands of opposition forces commanded by former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and his powerful ally, northern Uzbek General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
